content: 1. Flurbiprofen and Ciprofloxacin: The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. The mechanism is not well understood, but there is an increased risk of central nervous system (CNS) stimulation and seizures, particularly with high doses of fluoroquinolones. 2. Ciprofloxacin and Foscarnet: This interaction is considered minor, with an unknown mechanism. Based on case reports, there is a potential increased risk of seizures. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Fostamatinib and Ciprofloxacin: Fostamatinib may increase the levels or effects of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution is advised, and monitoring for toxicities of P-gp substrate drugs is recommended. Dosage adjustments may be necessary. 4. Ciprofloxacin and Fostemsavir: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. QTc prolongation has been reported with higher-than-recommended doses of fostemsavir. 5. Ciprofloxacin and Frovatriptan: Ciprofloxacin may increase the levels or effects of frovatriptan by inhibiting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This interaction is considered minor, but its clinical significance is unknown. Close monitoring is recommended. 6. Ciprofloxacin and Gemtuzumab: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Ciprofloxacin and Gepirone: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Therapy modification or close monitoring is recommended. 8. Ciprofloxacin and Gilteritinib: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ciprofloxacin and Givinostat: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is considered serious, and alternative drugs should be used if possible. If coadministration is unavoidable, obtain ECGs at baseline, during treatment, and as clinically indicated. Withhold treatment if the QTc interval exceeds 500 ms or if there is a change from baseline greater than 60 ms. 10. Ciprofloxacin and Glasdegib: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. If coadministration is unavoidable, monitor for an increased risk of QTc prolongation. 11. Glecaprevir/Pibrentasvir and Ciprofloxacin: Glecaprevir/pibrentasvir may increase the levels or effects of ciprofloxacin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Ciprofloxacin and Glimepiride: Ciprofloxacin may enhance the effects of glimepiride through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia have been reported in patients treated with quinolones and antidiabetic agents. Careful monitoring of blood glucose levels is recommended. 13. Ciprofloxacin and Glipizide: Ciprofloxacin may enhance the effects of glipizide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia have been reported in patients treated with quinolones and antidiabetic agents. Careful monitoring of blood glucose levels is recommended. 14. Ciprofloxacin and Glyburide: Ciprofloxacin may enhance the effects of glyburide through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Both hyperglycemia and hypoglycemia have been reported in patients treated with quinolones and antidiabetic agents. Careful monitoring of blood glucose levels is recommended. 15. Goserelin and Ciprofloxacin: Goserelin may increase the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. There is an increased risk of torsades de pointes. 16. Granisetron and Ciprofloxacin: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ciprofloxacin and Green Tea (Caffeine): Ciprofloxacin may increase the levels of green tea (caffeine) by decreasing its elimination. Some quinolones can inhibit the hepatic clearance of caffeine. Caution is advised. 18. Ciprofloxacin and Haloperidol: Both drugs can prolong the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. Ciprofloxacin has minimal effects on the QT interval, but caution is advised when used with other QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors. 19. Histrelin and Ciprofloxacin: Histrelin may increase the toxicity of ciprofloxacin by prolonging the QTc interval. Use caution and monitor closely. There is an increased risk of torsades de pointes. 20. Hydrocortisone and Ciprofloxacin: The coadministration of quinolone antibiotics and corticosteroids may increase the risk of tendon rupture. Use caution and monitor closely.
